record.paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
record.original_question: How can operation and maintenance processes for safety-critical machine-learning systems continuously check consistency between current operational data and the originally assumed test-data distribution, and update or adapt models when operational data changes over time?

evidence.quote: Operational data tend to change with time, creating a major problem for the operation and maintenance of machine-learning models [21]. In this way, the deviation between test data used during development and operation data becomes large as time elapses from completion of development. It is important to check the consistency between the operational data and the test data (originally assumed environment), and to make the machine-learning models follow the operational data in a continuous maintenance process.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a supervised machine-learning system deployed in a safety-critical setting. During development, the model is trained and validated on data drawn from a fixed but unknown distribution P_test on an input–output space X × Y. After deployment, the system observes a stream of operational inputs (and, possibly delayed or partially observed, corresponding outputs) (x_t, y_t)_{t≥1} drawn from a time-varying operational distribution P_op,t that may drift away from P_test as t grows.

Develop a principled methodology for the operation and maintenance phase that simultaneously:

1. (Consistency monitoring) Provides a statistical procedure that, at each time t, tests the null hypothesis H_0: P_op,t = P_test against the alternative of drift, with controlled false-alarm rate and quantifiable detection delay, using only the streaming operational data and a finite reference sample from P_test.

2. (Adaptation) Specifies a continuous update rule that modifies the deployed model f_t whenever significant drift is detected (or continuously), in such a way that
   (a) the updated model's risk under P_op,t is bounded above by a prescribed safety threshold,
   (b) safety-relevant performance guarantees established at development time are preserved or re-established under the updated distribution, and
   (c) the procedure is robust to label scarcity, label delay, and adversarial or rare-event inputs.

Formulate precise sufficient conditions on P_test, the family {P_op,t}, the model class, and the available feedback under which such a monitoring-and-adaptation scheme exists, and characterize fundamental limits (in terms of detection delay, sample complexity, and post-update risk) on any scheme satisfying the above safety requirements.
artifact.category_tag: Distribution shift detection and continual learning
artifact.status_search_result: Concept/data drift detection and safe continual adaptation for deployed ML systems remain active research areas. While many algorithms exist (e.g., ADWIN, DDM, MMD-based two-sample tests, conformal change detection, online learning under covariate shift), no general methodology provides certified safety guarantees for arbitrary safety-critical ML systems under non-stationary operational data. Recent surveys on concept drift, distribution-shift monitoring, and assurance of safety-critical ML continue to list this as an open challenge.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on Concept Drift Adaptation
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys methods for detecting and adapting to concept drift in evolving data streams; notes lack of unified framework with guarantees.
status_evidence.claim: General drift detection and adaptation in streaming ML is an active, unresolved research area.

status_evidence.title: Assurance of Machine Learning for Use in Autonomous Systems (AMLAS)
status_evidence.snippet: Guidance for assuring ML in safety-critical contexts highlights operational monitoring and updating as open assurance challenges.
status_evidence.claim: Continuous monitoring/updating with safety assurance is identified as an unresolved engineering and methodological problem.
